domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: The canonical per-employee, per-leave-type, per-accrual-period balance. `available` is a derived projection (entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays), computed server-side and never stored.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalanceView
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable wire projection of a LeaveBalance for the signed-in employee, carrying the full four-component breakdown (entitled, used, pending, available) plus the period window. It is a read-only view; no lifecycle.

domain_entities.name: DashboardBalanceDisplay
domain_entities.purpose: The dashboard's leave-balance presentation state. It resolves to exactly one of four mutually exclusive states derived from the two independent fetches (profile and balances), so a balances-only failure can never masquerade as a perpetual loading state.

business_rules: available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays. This is the single canonical derivation of the available balance; it is computed once (server-side in getCurrentBalances) and every consumer — including the dashboard — displays that value verbatim, never recomputing it locally. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance.available appears, not only here]

The full balance breakdown is entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays, and available, in that order, per leave type. A balance display that shows only `available` is incomplete: the user cannot tell whether they have taken 8 of 20 or 18 of 30, and pendingDays is the component most often surprising. Every balance presentation must render all four components. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalanceView presentation appears, not only here]

The dashboard balance display has exactly four mutually exclusive states: LOADING (either fetch in flight and no error), ERROR (either fetch failed), EMPTY (both fetches succeeded and balances is an empty array), and POPULATED (both fetches succeeded and balances is non-empty). EMPTY is a normal, expected outcome (e.g. a new joiner with no accrual period yet), not a rendering fault, and must be visibly distinct from both LOADING and ERROR. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever DashboardBalanceDisplay appears, not only here]

The profile fetch and the balances fetch are independent. A failure of the balances fetch alone must surface as ERROR, never as a permanently loading page. The loading condition must not be `employee === null || balances === null` (which conflates the two); it must be derived so that a balances-only failure resolves to ERROR. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever DashboardBalanceDisplay loading/error derivation appears, not only here]

An empty balances array (no balance rows for the employee's current accrual periods) is a valid, non-error result and must be rendered as an explicit empty state, never as an empty list that reads as a rendering fault. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalanceView[] (empty collection) appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Domain slice for the dashboard leave-balance breakdown + empty state.

Entities (no persistence/API concerns — those belong to data/application architects):
- LeaveBalance (existing, canonical): id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays, available (computed). Lifecycle OPEN | CLOSED (unchanged; OPEN/CLOSED is inferred from periodStart/periodEnd vs now, never stored).
- LeaveBalanceView (existing wire projection): the full four-component breakdown plus period window; immutable read-only view, no lifecycle.
- DashboardBalanceDisplay (new presentation state): balances, loading, error. Lifecycle LOADING | ERROR | EMPTY | POPULATED — four mutually exclusive states.

Binding business rules (scope broad):
- available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays is the single canonical derivation, computed server-side; the dashboard displays it verbatim and never recomputes locally (no second copy of the rule).
- The full breakdown is entitled, used, pending, available in that order per leave type; showing only `available` is incomplete.
- The dashboard has exactly four states; EMPTY is a normal outcome (new joiner, no accrual period) and must be visibly distinct from LOADING and ERROR.
- Profile and balances fetches are independent; a balances-only failure must resolve to ERROR, never a perpetual loading state (the `employee === null || balances === null` conflation is forbidden).
- An empty balances array is a valid non-error result rendered as an explicit empty state.

No new lifecycle states beyond DashboardBalanceDisplay's four; LeaveBalance OPEN/CLOSED is pre-existing and unchanged. No new day-count/rounding/unit boundaries are introduced — the canonical inclusive day-count (requestedDays) and available derivation already exist and are reused, not re-asserted narrowly.
